proposals.hole: PANEL-B1 binds gate evidence to a declared head SHA but does not bind the reviewed artifact bytes to that head, so dirty or substituted content can be reviewed using green evidence from different bytes.

proposals.hole: A mixed target can provide evidence for only one partition because the criteria do not explicitly require profile resolution and complete gate evidence independently for every class partition.

proposals.hole: PANEL-B2 records a recommending model but does not require that model to be outside the reviewing session's vendor family or at the routing table's mid tier.

proposals.hole: Subtract-only validation is measured against the class roster, so staffing can exceed the selected profile's default staffing or force ceiling while still passing PANEL-B2.

proposals.hole: An exclusion rationale need only exist; a placeholder such as a period can silently remove an applicable security lens.

proposals.hole: Delta scoping does not require the previously judged head to be an ancestor of the new head, so an unrelated or rewritten history can yield a misleading partial diff.

proposals.hole: Terminal-clean can be declared from a clean sweep even if the target changes after the sweep because PANEL-B4 does not bind the terminal declaration to the swept head.

proposals.hole: A typed-code mechanical finding can be marked fixed using a prose assertion that a test failed and passed; PANEL-B5 does not require an execution record comparable to precondition evidence.

proposals.hole: A transferred disposition only carries a work-item-shaped string; a nonexistent, closed-without-remediation, or unrelated item can satisfy the record shape.

dispositions.rationale: Settled, implemented B1 ground: the dispatch gate records the working directory of every claim, the emitter refuses unsynced bases, and verdict validity is keyed to head_sha. Whether the implemented emitter also binds dirty working-tree bytes is a code question for the whole-skill review campaign, not a criterion this amendment mints.
Covered: §4 partitions a mixed target per class, and each partition resolves its own profile with its own precondition set — B1's per-profile gate evidence therefore validates per partition already.

Rejected with p36 (same hole): the record names the recommending model precisely so foreignness is auditable afterwards; mechanical vendor-family validation needs a vendor registry the design deliberately does not own — routing tables move underneath it. Settled, implemented B2 ground.

Rejected with p32 (same hole): §4 binds staffing below the profile force ceiling normatively, and the deployed contract states the emitter checks the record against the roster and the force ceiling. Settled B2 ground; the whole-skill campaign judges the implemented check as code.

The two-layer seam — mechanical presence, audit-enforced quality — is the design's stated decision wherever a rationale appears (B4 names it a deliberate seam). A mechanical meaning-checker for rationales is itself an unbounded judgment problem.

In a non-interactive run the recommendation is the decision by definition (§4: record the recommendation and proceed); a record diverging from its own recommendation is a forged record, which criteria text cannot stop, and the verdict validates against the record either way.
Settled B3 ground: the emitter refuses unsynced bases; its behaviour over rewritten history is an implementation question the whole-skill campaign reviews as code.

Covered: verdict validity is keyed to head_sha, so a terminal-clean at H is stale and absent at any later head; across circuits, the accepted p33 makes post-termination change consume a re-arm before the campaign may terminate.
